patient.name: Denise Harrington
patient.chief_complaint: Two years of progressive bilateral foot numbness and burning, normal nerve tests
patient.hpi: Denise Harrington is a 48-year-old high school teacher presenting for a second neurological opinion after 2 years of progressively worsening bilateral foot and lower leg numbness and burning pain that is worse at night. She has been evaluated by two prior neurologists and a podiatrist, and has had three normal EMG/NCS studies, leading to frustration and the suggestion that her symptoms are 'anxiety-related.' She categorically denies anxiety as the explanation and presents with a self-documented 2-year symptom diary. The pain wakes her from sleep nightly and prevents her from wearing shoes for more than 2 hours. She has had complete lab work twice (HbA1c 5.6% — prediabetic range, B12 normal, TSH normal) which was attributed to mild prediabetes. She reports that the numbness began in the plantar surface of both feet and has crept up both legs, reaching mid-calf. Temperature sensation is markedly reduced (she scalds her feet in hot baths without noticing). Notably, she has normal balance and does not drop things — motor and large fiber function appear intact clinically. She recently read about 'small fiber neuropathy' online and has brought printouts asking about skin biopsy. She has no diabetes on fasting glucose, no alcohol, no relevant toxic exposures, and no family history of neuropathy. She has had dry eyes for 6 years treated with cyclosporine drops. She had a miscarriage 4 years ago attributed to 'unknown causes.' She takes no medications beyond cyclosporine ophthalmic.
pmh: Dry eye syndrome — bilateral (6 years, on topical cyclosporine)
Spontaneous miscarriage at 10 weeks gestation (4 years ago)
Recurrent aphthous mouth ulcers (2-3 per year since her 30s)
patient.review_of_systems: Positive: bilateral foot burning and numbness (worse at night), temperature loss, dry eyes (chronic), recurrent oral ulcers (2-3/year), prior miscarriage. Negative: weakness, ataxia, falls, hand symptoms, bowel/bladder dysfunction, joint swelling, rash, dry mouth.

family_history: Mother: type 2 diabetes. Father: hypertension. No family history of neuropathy or autoimmune disease.

social_history.note: High school biology teacher. Married, 2 children. Non-smoker. Rare alcohol (2-3 drinks per month). No illicit drugs. No occupational neurotoxin exposures.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: HbA1c 5.6 % (H), ESR 22 mm/hr (H), ANA 1:80 homogeneous titer (H), Anti-SSA (Ro) POSITIVE — 142 U/mL  (H), Anti-SSB (La) Positive — 28 U/mL  (H), Anti-phospholipid antibody (ELISA) IgG 28 GPL units (positive >40 GPL) GPL (H), Lupus anticoagulant POSITIVE  (H).

report.summary: NCS/EMG NORMAL — fourth normal study. This is expected for small fiber neuropathy. Standard NCS tests large myelinated (A-beta) fibers only. Small fiber (C and A-delta) pathology is invisible to NCS. The pattern of burning pain, allodynia, temperature loss with PRESERVED reflexes, vibration, proprioception, and normal NCS is DIAGNOSTIC of small fiber neuropathy pending skin biopsy confirmation.

emg.summary: ENTIRELY NORMAL. This does not exclude small fiber neuropathy.

report.overall_impression: NORMAL LARGE FIBER NCS/EMG. Skin punch biopsy for IENFD is the gold standard diagnostic test for small fiber neuropathy. Normal NCS in this clinical context is EXPECTED, not reassuring.

report.summary: Skin punch biopsy bilateral distal leg and proximal thigh. Anti-PGP9.5 immunostaining.

results.right_distal_leg_IENFD: 1.8 fibers/mm (reference age/sex-matched: 6.8-11.2 fibers/mm) — SEVERELY REDUCED, below 5th percentile
results.right_proximal_thigh_IENFD: 4.2 fibers/mm (reference: 8.4-16.8 fibers/mm) — MODERATELY REDUCED, below 5th percentile
results.sweat_gland_innervation: Markedly reduced sweat gland innervation bilaterally at distal leg

report.interpretation: SMALL FIBER NEUROPATHY CONFIRMED BY IENFD. Distal IENFD 1.8 fibers/mm (normal >6.8) — severely reduced. Length-dependent pattern. Combined with anti-SSA 142 U/mL positive and Sjögren's syndrome confirmation, this represents SJÖGREN'S SYNDROME-ASSOCIATED SMALL FIBER NEUROPATHY. Additional APS co-contribution cannot be excluded given lupus anticoagulant positivity.

report.summary: Minor salivary gland biopsy: focus score 1.5 foci/4 mm². Lymphocytic sialadenitis present. Combined with anti-SSA 142 U/mL, meets 2016 ACR/EULAR criteria for primary Sjögren's syndrome (score 6 — threshold ≥4).
report.interpretation: PRIMARY SJÖGREN'S SYNDROME confirmed. Neuropathy mechanism: Sjögren's small fiber neuropathy (immune-mediated dorsal root ganglion and small fiber involvement). Dry eye syndrome (6 years) is the index extraglandular manifestation. Treatment: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily for Sjögren's + symptom management for SFN pain (duloxetine, pregabalin).

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: Lupus anticoagulant (repeat) POSITIVE — confirmed persistent  (H), Anti-cardiolipin IgG (repeat) 32 GPL units (low positive) GPL (H), Anti-beta2-glycoprotein I IgG 28 U/mL U/mL (H).

report.summary: QST bilateral feet: Warm Detection Threshold (WDT): 47.2°C right, 47.8°C left (normal <40.5°C) — SEVERELY ELEVATED (loss of warm perception). Cold Detection Threshold (CDT): 23.4°C right, 22.8°C left (normal >28.4°C) — ELEVATED (loss of cold perception). Vibration Detection Threshold: 5.2 Hz right, 5.4 Hz left (normal <8 Hz) — NORMAL. Mechanical Pain Threshold: reduced (hyperalgesia) — 0.08 mN (normal 28-112 mN). Thermal pain threshold: allodynia to heat confirmed (painful at 38°C).
report.interpretation: QST confirms small fiber (A-delta and C fiber) dysfunction: loss of warm and cold detection with NORMAL vibration. Thermal hyperalgesia and mechanical hyperalgesia (allodynia) explain the clinical pain. Pattern consistent with Sjögren's SFN.

output.test_type: Autonomic Testing (QSART, TST, HRV, Tilt Table)

report.summary: QSART bilateral feet: absent (0 uL). QSART bilateral legs: severely reduced (0.14 uL, reference >0.40). Thermoregulatory sweat test: anhidrosis bilateral feet and lower legs. Orthostatic vitals: BP 122/76 supine, 108/70 at 3 min standing, 102/68 at 5 min — BORDERLINE ORTHOSTATIC HYPOTENSION (borderline definition: 20 mmHg systolic change, exactly met). HRV: mildly reduced low-frequency/high-frequency ratio. Findings: severe sudomotor small fiber dysfunction with borderline cardiovascular autonomic involvement.
report.interpretation: Severe autonomic small fiber involvement (sudomotor) with borderline orthostatic hypotension — consistent with Sjögren's SFN with autonomic component. Orthostatic symptoms should be monitored. Salt + water intake increase; compression stockings if orthostasis progresses.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Sjögren's syndrome-associated small fiber neuropathy with antiphospholipid syndrome overlap
critical_actions: VALIDATE symptoms — multiple 'normal NCS' does not mean no neuropathy; order skin biopsy
Order anti-SSA/SSB and antiphospholipid antibodies (lupus anticoagulant + anti-cardiolipin + anti-beta2GP1) — the key diagnostic tests missed previously
Skin punch biopsy for IENFD — the only objective test for SFN that will confirm the diagnosis
Confirm lupus anticoagulant positivity at 12 weeks (APS criteria require 2 tests 12 weeks apart)
Do not dismiss as psychiatric — IENFD reduced is an objective structural finding
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute symptoms to prediabetes (HbA1c 5.6%) or anxiety — both lead to delay in diagnosis
Do not perform another NCS instead of skin biopsy — NCS cannot detect small fiber neuropathy
Do not give IVIG without checking serum IgA (IgA deficiency is IVIG contraindication)
Do not withhold anticoagulation discussion — lupus anticoagulant + prior miscarriage meets APS obstetric criteria

differential.key_distinguishing: HbA1c 5.6% borderline prediabetes is extremely unlikely to cause this severity of small fiber loss at age 48; anti-SSA and APS serology point to autoimmune etiology; prediabetes cannot explain IENFD <2 fibers/mm
Autoimmune diagnoses (Sjögren's + APS) have been established; idiopathic is a diagnosis of exclusion after these are ruled out
IENFD objectively severely reduced on skin biopsy — structural test; QST objectively abnormal; this is organic small fiber neuropathy not psychiatric
Anti-dsDNA negative; anti-Smith negative; does not currently meet 4/11 ACR SLE criteria; APS + Sjögren's overlap is the more parsimonious diagnosis; monitor for SLE development

key_reasoning_points: DIAGNOSTIC PUZZLE: Triple diagnostic challenge — (1) normal NCS leading to psychiatric misattribution, (2) borderline prediabetes as convenient (but wrong) explanation, (3) overlooked Sjögren's features in plain sight (dry eye 6 years, recurrent oral ulcers, prior miscarriage)
KEY PRINCIPLE: Normal NCS does NOT exclude neuropathy — only large fiber (A-beta) function is tested; C and A-delta (pain, temperature) fibers are completely invisible to standard NCS
SJÖGREN'S SFN: Well-documented association; prevalence of neuropathy in Sjögren's ~20%; SFN is the most common phenotype (burning pain + temperature loss + normal NCS + normal reflexes)
APS CLUE: Prior miscarriage (obstetric criterion) + recurrent oral ulcers (SLE-spectrum) + lupus anticoagulant positive — overlooked in prior workups
DIAGNOSTIC TRAP: 3 normal NCS from 2 prior neurologists reinforced misattribution to anxiety; the mistake was not performing skin biopsy
Prior dry eye attributed to 'keratoconjunctivitis sicca' was a missed opportunity to test anti-SSA/SSB 6 years ago
